subject: Vocabulary
topic: Proverbs — Meaning and Contextual Application (W12 B1)

questions.stem: What does the proverb 'All that glitters is not gold' mean?

options.option_text: Precious metals are the most valuable assets
Everything that appears attractive or valuable may not actually be so
Hard work always leads to wealth
Beautiful things should be carefully preserved

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'All that glitters is not gold' = appearances can be deceptive; something that looks good on the surface may not be genuinely valuable or trustworthy. From Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice: 'All that glitters is not gold; often have you heard that told.' Use: 'The job offer seemed perfect, but all that glitters is not gold — the terms were exploitative.' Trap: 'precious metals most valuable' = literal reading (wrong; it's a metaphor about deception).

questions.stem: What does 'A stitch in time saves nine' advise?

options.option_text: Sewing is an important skill to learn
Time management is the key to productivity
Attending to problems early prevents greater effort later
Nine small tasks are better than one large task

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'A stitch in time saves nine' = dealing with a problem immediately, while it is small, prevents it from becoming much bigger and harder to handle. Origin: mending a small tear (one stitch) prevents it from tearing further (requiring nine stitches). Use: 'Get that leak repaired immediately — a stitch in time saves nine.' Trap: 'time management' = vaguely related but misses the core meaning of 'early intervention prevents escalation'; 'nine tasks better than one' = literal misreading.

questions.stem: What does 'The early bird catches the worm' mean?

options.option_text: Birds that wake early get more food
Those who start early or act promptly are more likely to succeed
Morning hours are best for physical activity
Punctuality is a virtue respected by employers

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'The early bird catches the worm' = those who begin promptly or arrive/start before others have an advantage and are more likely to achieve their goals. Use: 'I always arrive at job fairs early — the early bird catches the worm.' Trap: 'birds that wake early get more food' = literal reading of the metaphor (correct in nature but not the figurative meaning); 'morning hours best for physical activity' = health advice, not the proverb's intended meaning.

questions.stem: A student said 'I've already planned what to do with my expected scholarship.' His mentor replied, 'Don't count your chickens before they hatch.' What did the mentor mean?

options.option_text: Farming skills are important for financial security
You should not make plans at all for the future
Do not assume that expected good outcomes will definitely occur
Only hatch the most promising plans

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Don't count your chickens before they hatch' = do not make plans based on something good that hasn't happened yet and may not happen. Just because eggs are laid doesn't mean all will hatch. Use: 'I know you expect to win the contract, but don't count your chickens — several competitors are also bidding.' Trap: 'no future planning at all' = too extreme; the proverb warns against assuming success, not against planning; 'farming skills' = literal reading.

questions.stem: What does 'Every cloud has a silver lining' mean?

options.option_text: Weather patterns indicate future opportunities
Every difficult or negative situation has some positive aspect
Rich people can turn any situation to their advantage
Nature provides metaphors for understanding life

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Every cloud has a silver lining' = even the worst situations contain something hopeful or positive if you look hard enough. The image: storm clouds are dark, but their edges (linings) can appear silver when sunlight shines behind them. Use: 'Losing the job was hard, but every cloud has a silver lining — she discovered her true passion during the break.' Trap: 'weather patterns' = literal misreading; 'rich people' = nothing in the proverb refers to wealth.

questions.stem: What is the meaning of 'Rome was not built in a day'?

options.option_text: Ancient empires required military conquest
Important achievements and lasting structures require time and patience
Rome is the greatest city ever built by humans
Construction projects always face unexpected delays

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Rome was not built in a day' = significant accomplishments cannot be rushed; they require sustained effort over time. Rome's greatness was built over centuries. Use: 'Learning a language takes years — Rome was not built in a day.' Trap: 'military conquest' and 'greatest city' = historical facts not the figurative meaning; 'construction delays' = a literal misreading (the proverb is about patience and long-term effort, not delays specifically).

questions.stem: What does 'Necessity is the mother of invention' mean?

options.option_text: Mothers are the most inventive members of a family
Need or pressure is what drives people to create solutions
Inventions are only made when governments fund research
Basic needs must be met before luxury items are produced

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Necessity is the mother of invention' = when people face an urgent need, they are driven to find creative solutions. 'Necessity' (need) is the cause ('mother') that produces invention. Use: 'Faced with no clean water, villagers invented a simple filtration system — necessity is the mother of invention.' Trap: 'mothers are most inventive' = literal gender reading; 'government funding' = an external condition not mentioned in the proverb's philosophy.

questions.stem: A student who failed the exam in December appeared again in March and passed. His friend said 'Better late than never.' What did this mean?

options.option_text: March is a better month for exams than December
Time of arrival is more important than arrival itself
It is better to achieve something late than not to achieve it at all
Persistence in the face of failure is rare

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Better late than never' = it is preferable to do or achieve something after a delay than to fail to do it at all. The student succeeded eventually — though delayed — which is still better than not succeeding. Use: 'He submitted the assignment two days late, but better late than never.' Trap: 'March vs December' = literal calendar reading; 'persistence is rare' = while true, not what this specific proverb means.

questions.stem: What does 'Actions speak louder than words' mean?

options.option_text: Shouting is more effective than quiet conversation
Verbal communication is overrated in business
What a person does reveals their character more truly than what they say
People who act quickly are always more successful

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Actions speak louder than words' = what people do is a better indicator of their true intentions, character and commitment than what they merely promise or declare. Promises are easy; actions require effort and reveal sincerity. Use: 'He claimed to support the team, but never showed up to practice — actions speak louder than words.' Trap: 'shouting is more effective' = literal reading of 'louder'; 'quick action = success' = speed is not the point — truthfulness/character is.

questions.stem: What does 'A penny saved is a penny earned' mean in the context of personal finance?

options.option_text: Saving old coins is a profitable hobby
Earning high wages is easier than saving money
Reducing expenditure has the same financial value as earning additional income
Banks offer better returns than spending on consumer goods

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'A penny saved is a penny earned' = money that you save is as valuable as money you earn; avoiding unnecessary expenses is economically equivalent to generating income. In personal finance: cutting costs by Rs.1,000 = same net benefit as earning Rs.1,000 more (since you don't pay tax on savings but do on income — actually you come out ahead by saving). Use: 'I packed lunch instead of eating out — a penny saved is a penny earned.' Trap: 'coin collecting' = literal reading; 'earning high wages is easier' = the proverb says saving is AS valuable as earning, not which is easier.
